sections.h2: Where is Madison County, Iowa, and which towns are in it?
sections.html:
Madison County sits in south-central Iowa, covers about 562 square miles, and counted 16,548 residents in the 2020 census. Winterset is both the county seat and the largest city.

The county touches Dallas, Warren, Clarke, Union and Adair counties, and it meets Polk County at a single corner point. Interstate 80 clips the far northwest corner, while U.S. Highways 6 and 169 and Iowa Highway 92 carry most local traffic. A seller here is often dealing with a small town or an acreage, not a subdivision lot, so the parcel and the town both matter to a buyer.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Madison County?
sections.html:
Madison County was formed on January 13, 1846, and began governing itself in 1849. It carries the name of President James Madison, and Hiram Hurst is credited as the first European-American settler, arriving from Missouri around April 1846.

Winterset itself was platted in the summer of 1849. Its planned name was Summerset, but the commissioners switched it to Winterset after a stretch of unseasonably cold weather. The county courthouse there went up in 1868 and was rebuilt in 1876 after a fire.

Six of the county's original sixteen covered bridges still stand. The Roseman Covered Bridge appeared in the 1995 film The Bridges of Madison County, and the Holliwell Bridge did too. Winterset also holds the Covered Bridge Festival every second weekend in October, and the John Wayne Birthplace Museum opened there in 2015.

sections.h2: What should Madison County sellers know about storms, roads and the setting?
sections.html:
The most serious recent weather event in the county was a low-end EF4 tornado on March 5, 2022, which struck just outside Winterset and killed six people. Sellers with storm or hail damage should keep roofing and repair records, because buyers and lenders will ask for them.

  • Winterset sits in rolling farmland at about 1,099 feet of elevation, with the Middle River along its south side.
  • The county has a notable highway tunnel, Harmon Tunnel, cut through a meander of the Middle River in Pammel Park.
  • The Winterset Community School District runs the public schools in the county seat.
  • Real property here is reassessed every two years, so a sale price that differs from the county value is common and worth comparing.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Madison County?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, and both are in the Madison County Annex at 201 W. Court Avenue in Winterset. The Assessor sets the value of your property, and the Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

The Assessor's page lists Shawn Nigg as assessor and says real estate is revalued every two years with a January 1 effective date. Farm ground is valued by what it can produce, not by sale price. Parcel maps and records are on the county's assessor page, which links to the Beacon records site.

sections.h2: When can you protest a Madison County assessment?
sections.html:
You can file a written protest from April 2 through April 30 of the assessment year. Notices go out around April 1, and the Assessor's calendar also offers an informal review from April 2 to April 25 before you decide to file.

Under Iowa Code 441.37 you may protest on any of five grounds:

  • The value is unfair next to similar property in the same taxing district.
  • The value is higher than the law allows.
  • The property is exempt, not assessable or placed in the wrong class.
  • The assessment contains an error.
  • Fraud or misconduct, which the protest must describe specifically.

If you want an oral hearing, ask for it in writing when you file. A county placed under a disaster declaration can see the filing period move to May 1 through June 5.

sections.h2: Who sits on the Madison County Board of Review?
sections.html:
The Madison County Board of Review has three members: a farmer, a licensed real estate broker and a contractor, all from the county. The conference board appoints them, and the Assessor's office does not control their decisions.

The board meets from May 1 until it finishes, and state rules call for adjournment by May 31 unless the Department of Revenue extends the session. It sends a written decision with reasons. If you disagree, the next step is the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court, with a 20 day clock that starts at adjournment or May 31, whichever is later, according to the Department of Revenue's board of review summary.

In odd-numbered years there is also a protest window of October 9 through October 31 for owners hit by a state equalization order. The only argument allowed then is that the order pushes the value above actual value.

sections.h2: How do you pay Madison County property tax, and when is it late?
sections.html:
Iowa lets you pay the full year or two halves, and a half that is unpaid goes delinquent on October 1 or April 1. After that, interest runs at one and one-half percent a month, rounded to the nearest dollar with a $1 minimum, and any part of a month counts as a whole one (Iowa Code 445.39).

The county Treasurer takes payment at the annex, by mail with a check payable to the Treasurer, or online. The Treasurer's site says 2026/2027 statements are available. A senior or disabled owner can apply for the elderly and disabled homestead credit at the Treasurer by June 1 each year, according to the Madison County Treasurer.

A delinquency notice goes out if the first half is unpaid by February 1, and not receiving it does not excuse the payment, per the older Iowa Code chapter 445 text.

sections.h2: What happens if Madison County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The treasurer must offer parcels with delinquent taxes at the annual tax sale, held on the third Monday in June unless there is good cause for another June date (Iowa Code 446.7). Each parcel sells for the taxes, interest, fees and costs owed.

The original owner can still redeem after the sale. The redemption amount includes the sale price, a certificate fee and interest at two percent a month counted from the month of sale, under Iowa Code 447.1. Interest is costly, so settling the balance before June is the cheaper path.

sections.h2: What does a sale of a Madison County house involve for taxes?
sections.html:
A deed presented to the county recorder must come with a declaration of value signed by a buyer, a seller or an agent. The recorder passes the declaration to the assessor, who keeps it for three years after the year of transfer.

Iowa also charges a real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500, as set out in Iowa Code 428A.1. The statute section does not say which side pays, so your purchase contract decides that.

Property tax is a lien on the parcel, and unpaid amounts are normally cleared from the sale proceeds at closing. The homestead credit follows a similar timing rule: if a home sells before July 1, the new owner must file for the credit by July 1, but a sale after July 1 leaves the credit in place for that year, per the Iowa administrative rule.

sections.h2: What can Madison County sellers do about tax they owe?
sections.html:
Start with a payoff figure from the Treasurer at 515-462-1542, so you know the exact tax, interest and any fees on each parcel. Then decide how to use the sale to clear it.

  • Ask the Assessor for the parcel record and look for errors in square footage or class before April 30.
  • Gather sale prices for similar houses in Winterset, Earlham or your township if you plan to protest.
  • Report any removed or damaged buildings to the Assessor, since owners must report such changes.
  • Confirm in writing who pays transfer tax and the second-half tax before you sign.
  • Keep the Treasurer's receipt after closing as proof the parcel was clear.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Madison County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Winterset is the county seat and the largest city, with 5,353 people in the 2020 census. The Assessor and Treasurer both work from the Madison County Annex at 201 W. Court Avenue.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Madison County assessment?
faqs.a: April 30 of the assessment year, with filing open from April 2. An informal review with the Assessor is available April 2 through April 25, and a disaster declaration can move the deadline to June 5.

faqs.q: How often does Madison County revalue property?
faqs.a: Every two years, with a January 1 effective date, according to the county Assessor. Owners are asked to report new construction, remodels, finished basements, decks and any buildings removed or damaged.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the Madison County tax due date?
faqs.a: Interest starts at one and one-half percent a month after the October 1 or April 1 delinquency date. A parcel still unpaid can be offered at the June tax sale.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax when a Madison County house sells?
faqs.a: The statute sets the rate at 80 cents per $500 above the first $500 but does not say who pays. The purchase contract or local custom settles it, so ask your closing agent.
